profile.summary: This is a benchmark of taxonomic classification and profiling tools, not of models. Eleven methods, five of them written for long reads, were run on public mock community datasets sequenced with PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore and Illumina, where the species present and their intended abundances are known. Each method is scored on how many reads it uses, how precisely and completely it detects the known species, and how close its abundance estimates are to the manufacturer's specification.

summary_quotes.text: Here, we perform a critical benchmarking study using 11 methods, including five methods designed specifically for long reads.

We applied these tools to several mock community datasets generated using Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) HiFi or Oxford Nanopore Technology sequencing, and evaluated their performance based on read utilization, detection metrics, and relative abundance estimates.
The species compositions of the mock communities are known, allowing for a complete evaluation of detection metrics.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Three things per method and dataset. Read utilisation: what fraction of the reads the method assigns. Detection: precision, recall and F-score for the known species or genera, where a true positive is a mock community taxon whose read count passes a threshold and a false positive is any taxon not in the community. Abundance accuracy: the L1 distance between estimated and theoretical abundances, with a chi-squared goodness of fit test against the manufacturer's specification.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The datasets are public, empirical sequencing runs of commercial mock communities, chosen over simulations because simulations do not capture real error profiles, read length spread or extraction and library effects. They include a PacBio HiFi run of ATCC MSA-1003 (20 bacterial species in staggered abundances from 18% down to 0.02%; 2.4 million HiFi reads, median length 8.3 kb, 20.54 Gb) and a PacBio HiFi run of ZymoBIOMICS D6331 (17 species including one archaeon and two yeasts, staggered from 14% down to 0.0001%; 1.9 million reads, median 8.1 kb, 17.99 Gb), plus Oxford Nanopore R10 and Q20 runs of ZymoBIOMICS D6300 and Illumina runs of both communities. The truth is the species list and the manufacturer's stated genomic DNA abundances.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Materials and methods, Mock community datasets; Relative abundance estimates

quotes.text: We chose empirical datasets versus simulated datasets because simulations do not capture true variation in error profiles, read length heterogeneity, and the effects of DNA extraction, library preparation, and sequencing.
The ATCC MSA-1003 mock community contains 20 bacteria species in staggered abundances (5 species at 18%, 1.8%, 0.18% and 0.02% abundance levels, respectively).
The PacBio ATCC dataset was generated using the Sequel II System and contains 2.4 million HiFi reads with a median length of 8.3 kb, for a total of 20.54 Gb of data
The Zymo D6331 mock community contains 17 species (including 14 bacteria, 1 archaea, and 2 yeasts) in staggered abundances.
The theoretical abundances were obtained from the manufacturer’s specifications, which are based on genomic DNA (vs. cell counts).

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Presence or absence is scored against a minimum percentage of the dataset's total reads, not a fixed read count, because the datasets differ in size. Three thresholds are used: 0.001% (mild), 0.1% (moderate) and 1% (heavy); Table 3 gives the resulting read counts per dataset, for example 24 reads at 0.001% and 24,190 at 1% for HiFi ATCC MSA-1003. Scoring is done at both species and genus level. Abundances are normalised with all false positives summed into an 'Other' category, which is compared against a theoretical abundance of zero, and the chi-squared test uses a Bonferroni correction over the 11 methods, so the altered alpha is 0.0045.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: The paper prints the general command for each method, so a reader can repeat the analysis on the same public datasets. Kraken2 2.1.1 with the pre-built PlusPF database writes a kreport per sample; Bracken 2.6.0 then produces species-level abundances from that kreport. The other methods each have their own commands and databases in the same section. The kreport outputs, notebooks and results files are on the Open Science Framework project bqtdu.

limitations.text: Detection depends on an arbitrary percentage threshold, and the authors note this penalises methods that assign a smaller share of reads.

run_guide.summary: Download one mock community dataset and run the paper's own Kraken2 and Bracken commands on it.
prerequisites: Kraken2 version 2.1.1 and Bracken version 2.6.0, the versions the paper used.
The pre-built PlusPF database (RefSeq archaea, bacteria, viruses, plasmid, human, protozoa and fungi, released 27 January 2021).
One mock community dataset, for example HiFi ATCC MSA-1003 from NCBI SRX6095783, converted to FASTA.

# HiFi ATCC MSA-1003: NCBI PRJNA546278, run SRX6095783

steps.explanation: The paper names the accession for each dataset in its availability statement but gives no download command, so this step is an instruction rather than a command.
steps.source_locator: Paper: Availability of data and materials

quotes.text: HiFi ATCC MSA-1003 (NCBI: PRJNA546278: SRX6095783)

steps.title: Classify the reads with Kraken2
steps.explanation: The paper's Kraken2 command, copied as printed. Note that the report flag as printed in the article uses a non-standard dash character.

quotes.text: kraken2 --db PlusPF --threads 24 –report SAMPLE.kreport.txt SAMPLE.fasta
We ran Kraken version 2.1.1 for each sample.

steps.title: Estimate species abundances with Bracken
steps.explanation: The paper's Bracken command, which reads the Kraken2 report and gives species-level abundances.

quotes.text: bracken -d PlusPF -i SAMPLE.kreport.txt -o SAMPLE.bracken -r 50 -l S -t 10
We ran Bracken version 2.6.0 for each sample, using the kreport outputs from Kraken2.

outputs: A Kraken2 report (SAMPLE.kreport.txt) and read assignments (SAMPLE.kraken), then a Bracken species abundance table (SAMPLE.bracken). The authors' own kreport outputs for all methods and datasets are on the OSF project.
limitations: These commands were read from the paper and have not been executed by Rewire.
They cover two of the eleven methods; the paper gives separate commands and databases for the rest.
The paper provides no script that computes precision, recall or L1 distance from these outputs; the notebooks on OSF were not read.

notes: This record is one paper's evaluation of existing tools, not a released suite with a harness or leaderboard, so code_url is null and results_url points at the authors' OSF deposit, which the OSF API record shows as public, with a licence attached (OSF licence id 563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e973, year 2021) whose name is not in the saved record, so data_licence is null. size is the number of reads in each dataset as Table 3 prints it, not a count of scored examples. The six structured entries match the store's six protocols, all at the 0.001% species-level threshold; the paper also reports the 0.1% and 1% thresholds and genus-level results. The raw datasets themselves live at the NCBI, ENA and lab addresses in the availability statement, not on OSF; data_url is given as the OSF project because that is where the authors' processed outputs and results sit.
